paras: The killing of Mrs. Collins Summers and suicide of William Stull took place in April 1882 near North Georgetown, Columbiana County, Ohio, where Stull, a discharged farmhand, was accused of shooting his former employer's wife. The first wire reports said fifty men were searching the woods to lynch him, but when the county sheriff and deputies cornered him near New Franklin two days later, he shot himself. Mrs. Summers died of her wounds; none of the coverage states the race of anyone involved.

Stull had worked for a year or two as a hired hand for Collins Summers, described as one of the most prominent farmers of Columbiana County. Summers discharged him about ten days to two weeks before the shooting, "on account of his quarrelsome disposition" according to the Herald special, and Stull was said to blame Mrs. Summers for his dismissal. The Stark County Democrat gave his age as barely 23.

On Sunday, Stull approached Mrs. Summers while she was milking at the barn, greeted her, and then fired his revolver into her as she turned back to her work. The Canton local weekly reported five shots, three of which struck her, one in the spine causing paralysis. Stull fled, and a Columbus dispatch printed on April 25 said fifty men were scouring the woods "to lynch him."

Officers tracked him toward Osnaburg, and on Tuesday morning, April 25, the Columbiana County sheriff and six deputies surrounded him in woods near New Franklin, fourteen miles southeast of Canton. Finding escape impossible, he fired into his own head with the same revolver and died. A Georgetown wire said he shot himself "to prevent lynching."

The Herald special described the excitement in Stark and Columbiana counties as intense. Mrs. Summers was still alive in critical condition on April 27, and on May 11 the Stark County Democrat reported that her funeral had been held and was very largely attended. No report of an inquest into either death appears in the coverage.

The first report, a brief Columbus dispatch in the Wheeling papers headed "Murdered by a Tramp," called Stull a tramp refused work, placed the farm in Tuscarawas County, and treated the planned lynching as plain news. Fuller specials from Canton and New Comerstown the next day corrected these details and denounced Stull as a "vile wretch" and "inhuman monster," while noting without comment that "fears are entertained that he will be lynched if caught."

The Canton wire of his suicide ran as far as St. Paul and Yankton, and a Georgetown wire, which gave his name as "Strull" and the place as "Franklin, Pa.," appeared in Sacramento and Los Angeles. The fullest accounts came from Ohio papers, including the Canton weekly and the Woodsfield Spirit of Democracy, which called the shooting one of the most cowardly crimes ever committed in that section.

Reports differed on the details: the Georgetown wire said six shots killed Mrs. Summers instantly on Sunday evening, while the Ohio papers reported five shots on Sunday morning and her survival for some days. The first dispatch placed the farm in Tuscarawas County, but the Canton reports, closer to the scene, gave Columbiana County.

chips: Lynching of any race (not in the anti-Black count)
bases: The papers describe a farmhand's shooting of his former employer's wife and his suicide when a sheriff's posse cornered him, with lynching only threatened during the manhunt (A1, A5, A10); no race is stated for anyone.
Early reports said fifty men meant to lynch Stull (A1, A2), but he was cornered by the Columbiana county sheriff and deputies and killed himself before capture (A5, A10); no one was killed by a mob.

Independent dispatches from Columbus, Canton, New Comerstown and New Philadelphia and the Canton local weekly agree on the shooting of Mrs. Summers and Stull's suicide when cornered near New Franklin (A1, A5, A6, A10, A11).

accounts.gist: A tramp refused work shot Mrs. Sommers twice near North Georgetown, Tuscarawas county; fifty men were scouring the woods to lynch him.

accounts.label: Canton/Herald special
accounts.gist: A discharged hired hand, Stull, emptied his revolver into Mrs. Summers at the barn Sunday evening; cornered at sunrise near New Franklin by the sheriff and deputies, he shot himself dead.

accounts.label: Georgetown wire
accounts.gist: Strull shot Mrs. Summers six times, killing her instantly, and shot himself near Franklin, Pa., 'to prevent lynching'.

accounts.label: Ohio local and regional papers
accounts.gist: Five shots fired Sunday morning, three hit; Mrs. Summers lay in critical condition while Stull, tracked toward Osnaburg, was surrounded by the sheriff and six deputies and shot himself.

framing.detail: The first wire ('Murdered by a Tramp') reported the plan to lynch as a plain fact, without comment.
Later accounts condemned Stull as a 'vile wretch' and 'inhuman monster' and noted fears he would be lynched without disapproval.

conflicts.note: The Canton local weekly and the fuller specials give Columbiana; the brief first dispatch is likely mistaken.
